profile_text.body:
OpenAI is a for-profit AI company founded in 2015 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its primary consumer product is ChatGPT, which the company's website describes as a tool to answer questions, write, create images, complete work, and code, available for free or via a downloadable app. The site notes that chats may be reviewed and used to improve OpenAI's AI models.

Beyond ChatGPT, OpenAI offers a range of tracked products: the OpenAI API and GPT models for developers on a usage-based pricing structure, an API Playground and Dashboard for testing and fine-tuning, DALL-E for image generation, Sora for video generation, Whisper API for speech recognition and transcription, and Operator, an autonomous web agent capable of browser control and action authorization.

The held facts record substantial litigation exposure. OpenAI entities appear as defendants or parties in at least twelve cases across federal courts in California, New York, Florida, Hawaii, and Arkansas, including matters involving wikiHow, Inc., X.AI Corp., the Office of the Attorney General of the State of Florida, and two separate United States government filings in the Eastern District of Arkansas. California is identified as the jurisdiction with the highest case count associated with the company, at 161 matters. OpenAI also has a presence in the MCP server registry through several listed integrations.
